new_statements.quote: 3.1 Word & Syllable Structure. The phonological word may be monosyllabic or disyllabic. Disyllables are invariably iambic, comprising a prosodically prominent main syllable preceded by a prosodically non-prominent presyllable, which is comparatively restricted in terms of phonotactics and segment inventory. Monosyllables are structurally equivalent to main syllables. [...] Presyllables are structurally deficient compared with main syllables. They must contain two segments, either /CV/ or /CC/ [...] the vocalic presyllable rime /V/ is completely underspecified for vowel quality. It is typically realized as a short, mid to open central vowel
new_statements.citation: Gehrmann, Ryan. 2019. On the origin of rime laryngealization in Ta'oiq: a case study in the phonatory restructuring of vowel quality contrasts. Paper presented at ICAAL 8, Chiang Mai University.
new_statements.locator: Gehrmann 2024, ch.5 sec.3.1 'Word & Syllable Structure', book pp.27-28 (pp.41-42 of); scope statement p.26 (p.40): 'Ta'oiq subsumes a number of named doculects, including Ta'oiq [tth] (Conver et al. 2014; Gehrmann 2015), Ong [oog] (Ferlus 1974, 1979), Bru of Talan village (Huffman 1979a, Diffloth 1989), Ir [irr] (Huffman 1979b) and Katang (Ferlus 1974).'
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Re-opened from the mirror. Title page: 'Austroasiatic Linguistics, in honor of Gerard Diffloth (1939-2023)', ed. Paul Sidwell, ISBN 978-616-398-980-2, PDF version 24 October 2024; ch.5 pp.25-48 = Ryan Gehrmann, 'A Reconstruction of Proto-Ta'oi Phonology and Lexicon with a Focus on the Origins of Rime Laryngealization Contrasts' (CC-BY). The quoted passage stands verbatim at ch.5 sec.3.1 'Word & Syllable Structure', book pp.27-28 (the text; ellipses marked): 'The phonological word may be monosyllabic or disyllabic. Disyllables are invariably iambic, comprising a prosodically prominent main syllable preceded by a prosodically non-prominent presyllable..'. Scope sentence p.26 verbatim: 'Ta'oiq…
new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (irrr1240 has no catalog record and no stress statement held by the project). Consistent with the areal/general statements already noted on verification (Gehrmann 2022 thesis p.5-6: sesquisyllabic presyllable prosodically non-prominent; Sidwell 2005 Katuic word template without a stress statement) and now stated specifically for Ta'oiq, whose named doculects include Ir and Ong.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ta'oiq (the Ta'oi variety that explicitly includes the Ir [irr] and Ong [oog] doculects) has words of one or two syllables; every disyllable is iambic: prominence is on the final (main) syllable, the presyllable is prosodically non-prominent with a reduced/underspecified vowel (or a C+liquid shape). Prominence is therefore fixed on the word-final syllable and non-contrastive; the language's lexical suprasegmental contrast is register (modal vs creaky rime, plus rime-final glottalization), not stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: none mentioned (maximal word is a disyllable; no secondary prominence discussed)
new_statements.exceptions: none: 'Disyllables are invariably iambic'. Only phonotactic detail: /CC/ presyllables /pr tr cr kr kl/ surface with the excrescent vocoid after the liquid ([prᵊlɔː] 'flame'), /hr/ with it between the consonants; this does not affect prominence.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement is made for 'Ta'oiq', the conservative variety of the Ta'oi language of Salavan province, Laos, described from Conver et al.'s (2014) unpublished Ta'oiq [tth] lexicon and recordings; the author states (p.26) that Ta'oiq 'subsumes a number of named doculects, including Ta'oiq [tth], Ong [oog] (Ferlus 1974, 1979), Bru of Talan village (Huffman 1979a, Diffloth 1989), Ir [irr] (Huffman 1979b) and Katang (Ferlus 1974)', i.e. Ir (irrr1240, = Glottolog Ong-Ir ongg1239) is explicitly one of the doculects covered, though the primary data are from the [tth] doculect rather than from Ir speakers.

sources.note: Areal generalisation only, sec. 2.2 pp.5-6: in the MSEA sesquisyllable 'The penult, generally referred to as either the presyllable or minor syllable.., is prosodically non-prominent, being derived from the penult of a historical iambic disyllable'; tone/register culminative, one per word. Ta'oiq treated pp.~84-85 (Table 91, register-conditioned coda mutations citing Ferlus 1974a, Diffloth 1989, Gehrmann 2019); no Ong/Ir stress statement.

sources.citation: Schmutz, Jonathan. 2013. The Ta'oi language and people. Mon-Khmer Studies 42: i-xiii.
sources.note: Ethnonym/glossonym review only: Ir (Yir, In, Zir) and Ong (Tong, Hantong) as Ta'oi subgroups (Schliesinger 2003), Sidwell 2005 'Ong/Ir/Talan' one dialect; Table 3 lists Ong and Ir as 'dialects in need of data'; 'There seems to be at least an ethnographic difference between the Ta'oi and the Ir and Ong' (pp.ix-x). No phonology.

sources.note: Re-read p.16 (the only prose page): consonant/final/vowel charts; 'This language is Iir /jiir/ [dyi:r] (Lao In, Thomas and Headley Ir); it is very close to Lao Bru, possibly just a dialect'; glottalized vs plain vowel contrast, homorganic preocclusion before nasals, lax stops in nasal environment, Cr-/Cl- slight aspiration, 'a certain amount of alternation between Crə- and Cər- in presyllables'. Nothing on stress or accent.
